name: Film grain
one_line: Fine, shifting texture over the picture that mimics photographic emulsion
summary: A seeded, slightly soft texture sits over the image and changes from frame to frame, strongest in the mid-tones. It adds analogue warmth, ties synthetic layers into one surface and hides smooth-gradient banding. Plain digital noise reads as sensor fuzz or cheapness, and grain too fine for delivery simply disappears.

routes.one_line: Generate seeded grain per pixel in a shader and blend it over the frame

steps.does: Build seeded, softened noise from a frame-derived seed and add it, weighted by luminance

limits: WebGL evidence is a software-rendered triangle read back; no noise or blending is exercised
Grain size and survival after encode are yours to check

routes.one_line: Add temporal noise across a rendered clip in one filtergraph pass

steps.does: Apply a seeded noise filter to the finished video as a final pass

limits: FFmpeg evidence does not include a noise filter
A final pass hits everything, text included; it cannot target layers

routes.one_line: Make a set of grain plates, then composite one per frame over stills or frames

steps.does: Generate seeded, softened noise plates centred on neutral grey
Composite the plate for each frame over the artwork with a soft blend

limits: ImageMagick evidence covers solid frames, not noise generation
sharp evidence is one RGBA composite; blend modes beyond that are untested, and some are unsupported
A short plate set repeats visibly over a long clip
